Executive Summary

30%
of gross contribution margin is given back to returns — the single largest, most controllable margin leak in the business.
CAC is the real killer
22 of 28 loss-making SKUs are primarily CAC-driven, not returns-driven. The Influencer channel alone overspends its peer channels' typical CAC by ~₹26L.
28 SKUs + 1 channel
are currently loss-making after CAC, of 150 SKUs total. 12 more are trending negative — an early-warning list, not yet a crisis.
WAPE ~19%
demand-forecast error. The stockout-alert rule is tuned toward catching real risk (79% recall) over avoiding false alarms (27% precision) — a deliberate trade-off for an early-warning tool.

Honest Limitations

  • Forecasting the month right after a sale month carries a stated bias risk. A trailing moving average naturally absorbs a recent sale spike; a de-seasonalization step (see Stage 6) measurably reduces this but does not eliminate it — expect the July forecast and Stockout Risk count to run somewhat high following June's sale month.
  • The stockout-alert rule favors recall over precision by design (79% recall, 27% precision) — it is tuned to not miss real risk, at the cost of roughly 3 in 4 flags not corresponding to an actual recorded near-stockout event. Treat flags as a triage list for a merchandiser, not an auto-trigger for purchase orders.
  • The long tail of low-volume SKUs is inherently hard to forecast — a SKU selling 2-3 units a month has almost no signal to average, so its individual forecast error can be large even while the company-wide WAPE looks reasonable.
  • The seasonal adjustment factor rests on a single observed sale month (Nov 2025) inside the training window — a real business would refine this with 2-3+ years of promotional history.
